summary:
ORBITAL FRONTIER is a web-based space exploration and rocket simulation experience designed around the concept of becoming a spacecraft engineer and astronaut. The project combines a futuristic mission-control interface with 3D spaceflight, rocket engineering, planetary exploration, and astronaut-oriented gameplay.

The core idea is to let the player progress through a space mission by designing and configuring a spacecraft, preparing it for launch, controlling the mission, exploring space/planets, and completing scientific and engineering objectives.

For a hackathon presentation, you could describe it like this:
ORBITAL FRONTIER is an immersive 3D space exploration and rocket engineering simulator that transforms the player into both a spacecraft engineer and astronaut. Players can design and customize spacecraft, prepare missions, launch rockets, monitor flight telemetry, navigate through space, explore planetary environments, and complete engineering and scientific challenges. The project combines interactive 3D graphics, spacecraft systems, mission progression, and scientifically informed space data into a single browser-based experience.
details:
ORBITAL FRONTIER — BEYOND EARTH. BEYOND LIMITS.

Project Overview

ORBITAL FRONTIER is an interactive 3D space exploration and rocket engineering simulator that puts the player in the role of both a spacecraft engineer and astronaut.

The player can select a mission and destination, study environmental conditions, design and customize a spacecraft, select engines, fuel systems, structural components, thermal protection and scientific equipment, and perform pre-launch inspections.

The configured spacecraft is then used in a simulated mission involving rocket launch, atmospheric ascent, flight telemetry, stage separation, orbital navigation, spacecraft deployment, planetary missions, astronaut exploration, spacecraft repair, scientific sample collection and mission scoring.

The spacecraft configuration is connected to the simulation. For example, changing engines can affect thrust and fuel consumption, while adding additional protection increases vehicle mass. This makes engineering decisions part of the actual gameplay rather than purely cosmetic customization.

The first complete mission is designed around the Moon, where the player progresses from spacecraft preparation and launch through lunar operations, repairs and scientific objectives.

Benefits and Educational Value

ORBITAL FRONTIER combines education, engineering concepts and interactive gameplay.

Players can learn simplified concepts related to rocket propulsion, mass and thrust, fuel management, orbital mechanics, spacecraft systems, thermal protection, radiation, life support, planetary environments and mission planning.

Instead of simply reading about spaceflight, players make engineering decisions and see their consequences in the simulation.

For example:

  • More fuel increases capacity but also increases vehicle mass.
  • Different engines provide different thrust and fuel-consumption characteristics.
  • Additional shielding improves protection while adding mass.
  • Different spacecraft configurations can be better suited to different missions.

The project is also designed to incorporate reliable information from NASA, NOAA, JPL, ESA and other authoritative scientific sources rather than presenting fabricated scientific information.

Intended Impact

The intended impact of ORBITAL FRONTIER is to make space science and spacecraft engineering more accessible, interactive and engaging.

Many people experience space science through videos, articles or static educational material. ORBITAL FRONTIER attempts to bridge that gap by allowing users to experience the process themselves:

Design → Inspect → Launch → Fly → Explore → Discover

The project aims to encourage:

  • Interest in STEM
  • Curiosity about space science
  • Understanding of engineering trade-offs
  • Interest in aerospace engineering
  • Scientific thinking
  • Problem solving
  • Mission planning
  • Experimentation

The long-term vision is to expand the Moon mission architecture into missions involving Mercury, Venus, Mars and the outer planets, using appropriate orbital, atmospheric or robotic missions where conventional landing is scientifically inappropriate.

Technology and Development

ORBITAL FRONTIER is designed as a browser-based 3D application, allowing users to experience the project without installing a traditional desktop game.

The planned technology stack includes:

  • React — application and UI architecture
  • TypeScript — strongly typed application and game logic
  • Three.js — real-time 3D rendering
  • React Three Fiber — React integration for Three.js
  • Drei — reusable 3D utilities
  • Tailwind CSS — responsive interface styling
  • Zustand — centralized game-state management
  • Rapier or an appropriate browser physics system — physics-related simulation
  • GLTF/GLB assets — spacecraft and environmental models
  • Node.js or Python-based backend services, where required
  • NASA and other public scientific APIs/datasets for scientific information
  • Vercel — deployment and hosting

The project is designed to use optimized 3D assets, compression, level-of-detail rendering, frustum culling, lazy loading and adaptive graphics quality to improve browser performance.

Creativity and Innovation

The creativity of ORBITAL FRONTIER comes from combining several traditionally separate experiences into one interactive system.

Instead of creating only a rocket simulator, planet viewer, educational dashboard or astronaut game, ORBITAL FRONTIER combines them into a single mission experience.

The player moves between different roles:

SPACECRAFT ENGINEER — Design and configure the spacecraft.

FLIGHT ENGINEER — Inspect systems and monitor telemetry.

PILOT — Control the spacecraft during flight.

MISSION OPERATOR — Navigate and manage spacecraft systems.

ASTRONAUT — Explore, repair equipment and conduct scientific activities.

Another creative aspect is the modular spacecraft system, where components are intended to have actual consequences within the simulation rather than simply changing the appearance of the vehicle.

The project also combines real scientific information with simulated gameplay.

Information is explicitly distinguished as:

REAL DATA — retrieved from scientific sources.

SIMULATED — calculated by the game.

EDUCATIONAL MODEL — simplified representation of scientific principles.

This allows the project to remain engaging while maintaining scientific transparency.

Design Considerations

Several important factors were considered while designing ORBITAL FRONTIER.

Scientific accuracy: Real scientific information must be distinguished from game simulation, and fictional values should not be presented as actual NASA measurements.

Gameplay feasibility: A complete professional-grade space simulator would be extremely complex, so the project uses simplified educational simulation models while maintaining consistent relationships between variables.

Performance: Because the game runs in a browser, the project considers 3D asset size, rendering performance, loading times, texture optimization, level of detail, lazy loading and responsive design.

Usability: Complex spacecraft information needs to remain understandable, so telemetry, warnings, engineering statistics and mission information are organized into dedicated HUD and dashboard systems.

Modularity: The spacecraft, missions, planets, astronaut systems and simulation logic are designed as modular systems so additional missions can be added without rebuilding the entire application.

Scientific realism versus gameplay: The goal is not to claim that ORBITAL FRONTIER is a professional aerospace simulator. Instead, it aims to create a scientifically informed educational simulation that is also engaging and playable.

Hackathon constraints: The Moon mission was selected as the first complete vertical slice so the project can demonstrate the complete gameplay loop before expanding to additional planetary missions.

Project Vision

ORBITAL FRONTIER aims to transform space exploration from something users simply watch or read about into something they can actively experience.

The core experience is:

DESIGN → BUILD → LAUNCH → FLY → EXPLORE → DISCOVER

BEYOND EARTH. BEYOND LIMITS.
